title: Dependency, Network, Failure & Graceful-Degradation Runtime
objective: Implement engineering-domain dependency/network topology adapters, declared redundancy and alternate paths, bounded failure propagation, isolation and graceful-degradation interpretation, and setting-defined resource/control interface bindings without inventing unknown topology or taking generic graph/constraint-analysis authority from PCA-12/Packet-08.
acceptance: Failure propagates only along explicitly declared dependency relations.
Redundant or alternate paths prevent propagation only when definitions explicitly declare and satisfy them.
Coarse resource state such as power/fuel/heat/fluid/ammunition/data/control/magical supply does not imply finer network topology that is absent from source definitions.
Unknown or conflicting topology remains unresolved and blocks only operations requiring that topology.
Cycles and graph analyses are bounded, noncanonical engineering evidence rather than live owner state.
Isolation/graceful-degradation state comes only from declared engineering definitions and accepted owner evidence.
PCA-12/Packet-08 retain generic graph/constraint/formal-analysis machinery; MERA supplies model adapters and interpretation only.
Visibility filtering occurs before dependency/network lists, counts, graph extraction and analysis input.
Blocking network/failure workflows remain semantic/nonvisual and provider-off.
boundaries: PCA-12/Packet-08 retain generic graph, constraint, optimization and formal-analysis authority.
D17/PPIA-03 and MIB-14/PPIA-04/F014 retain live Asset/platform/resource/configuration state.
GPR + Action/Event retain generic execution/replay authority.
MERA cannot infer detailed circuit, bus, pipe, fuel, thermal, data, control or magical topology from a coarse resource label.
Unknown topology stays unknown; no universal cascade, redundancy or graceful-degradation formula is introduced.
MERA-12+ domain adapter work remains unauthorized.
MBES remains blocked until MERA completes at MERA-24.
